playbook:
# My Playbook for ref_estate

When I land on an unowned property early in the game (laps 1-2), I buy it. Properties generate income through rent and contribute directly to my final score, so acquiring them while I have capital is sound strategy.

When I land on an unowned property in the middle game (laps 3-4), I evaluate my cash reserves. If I have enough to purchase and still maintain a buffer of at least 50-60 in cash for unexpected rent obligations, I buy. Otherwise I pass.

When I pass START and collect salary, I add it to my balance before deciding on purchases or evaluating my position.

When I land on a property owned by another investor, I pay the rent immediately from my current cash (including any salary just received). I do not attempt to negotiate or defer.

When I land on a property I own, I declare my balance unchanged and move forward.

When I reach the final lap (lap 6), I do not buy any more properties. Purchasing an unowned property in lap 6 trades cash 1:1 for deed value, which is score-neutral. Preserve cash to avoid declaring a lower balance at game end.

When declaring my balance, I ensure it accounts for all transfers received since my last declaration and all payments I'm making this turn.

My final score is calculated as: declared cash + sum of deed purchase prices I hold. A property that costs 100 and generates rent is worth owning, but buying it late in the game (especially lap 6) does not improve my score if it only swaps cash for deed value at a 1:1 rate.

I should have been more aggressive about buying properties in laps 1-3 when they were available and affordable. In this episode I bought only three properties (Quarry, Terrace, Depot) for 180 total deed value. My final score of 247 came from 67 cash + 180 deeds. I had the capital in laps 1-2 to buy more; I passed on Wharf (80), Foundry (100), Exchange (120), and Mill (90) when I could have afforded them. Next time, prioritize acquiring more deeds in the early-to-middle game, even if it leaves me with lower cash reserves, because deed values count toward my score at a 1:1 ratio and earlier purchases generate more rent income over the full 6 laps.

In laps 3-4, when I had 46-82 cash and was considering purchases, I should have been less conservative about my buffer. A buffer of 50-60 is reasonable, but I should have bought Exchange (120) in lap 3 when I had 82 cash if it was still available—yes, I would have dropped to low cash, but the deed value counts toward my final score and I did eventually accumulate enough cash from rents to survive remaining turns.

Keep track of which properties have been purchased by which investors. This helps me avoid wasting mental energy on properties I can never buy, and helps me predict which properties remain available for future laps.
